planning_scheme.name: City of Mount Isa Planning Scheme 2020
planning_scheme.version: City of Mount Isa Planning Scheme 2020 (as commenced 09 March 2020; no amendment/version number published)
planning_scheme.notes: Council page (read via WebFetch) states Council 'adopted the City of Mount Isa Planning Scheme 2020 on 12 February 2020' and it commenced Monday 9 March 2020; it lists a Major Amendment planned for 2026-2027 (housing focus) but no amendment in force. Every page header of the official no-maps PDF reads 'City of Mount Isa Planning Scheme – 09 March 2020' (413 pages, PDF created 25 Feb 2020, modified 28 Feb 2020, author andrewstownplanning). The official council server (Akamai) returned 403 to every scripted client from this machine, so the official no-maps PDF was retrieved as a byte-for-byte Internet Archive capture of the council URL (snapshot 20250407213909, id_ raw mode; SHA-256 ca488ad3fb04c260acd7532ca3abf9c59d3ed2a313e45d8b4adc3485e7cd069b, 11,823,884 bytes). The live council page still links the same /v/1/ file name, so this is believed to be the current text. QHC: the scheme text contains no reference to the Queensland Housing Code (0 matches for 'Housing Code'); it refers only to the QDC. No QHC adoption found.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1 s1.6 says the scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work under ss32-33 of the Building Act 1975, and that the building assessment provisions in the scheme are the Low density residential zone and Medium density residential zone assessment of a Class 10A building. Table 5.7.1 makes construction of a Class 10a building in the Low density residential, Medium density residential and Township zones accepted subject to requirements, assessed against Residential activities code PO 22 and PO 23 only (domestic outbuildings / garages / carports / pools: height, size, garage location behind front building line or opening width). Neither PO 22 nor PO 23 states a numeric side or rear setback, so for stand-alone Class 10a building work QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 boundary clearances remain the operative side/rear setbacks. The Residential activities code AO 4.1 (road setback) and AO 4.2/Table 9.3.6.3 (side and rear) apply to 'buildings and other structures' when a residential use is assessed (MCU accepted subject to requirements or assessable), but Table 9.3.6.3 carries the note 'the Queensland Development Code setbacks apply for dwelling houses and dual occupancies'. The scheme does not mention the Queensland Housing Code.

quotes.text: This planning scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.
specify alternative boundary clearances and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33 of the Building Act 1975.

The building assessment provisions are contained in the following parts of this planning scheme: (a) Low density residential zone: assessment of a Class 10A building. (b) Medium density residential zone: assessment of a Class 10A building.
dwelling house | Accepted If in a residential zone and identified in schedule 6, part 2(2) of the Regulation | Editor’s note – the Queensland Development Code also applies to dwelling houses.
Note—the Queensland Development Code setbacks apply for dwelling houses and dual occupancies.

definitions.text: domestic outbuilding means a non-habitable class 10a building that is— (a) a shed, garage or carport; and (b) ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.

setback, for a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: One local plan: Mount Isa airport local plan (precincts: Airport operations; Commercial and low impact industry; Tourist and recreational; Aircraft manoeuvring; Western airport). Its code (Table 7.2.1.1 AO 1.4) sets building and structure setbacks (10 m Barkly Highway frontage, 6 m airport entry road, 4 m other road frontage, 2 m secondary frontage, 1.5 m side/rear) and prevails over other provisions, but Table 5.9.1 lists no Dwelling house in the local plan (only Caretakers accommodation), so it is not recorded as a Class 10 dwelling-house rule. Local plan codes prevail over zone and use codes (s1.5(1)(d)). Zone codes (Part 6) contain purpose and overall outcomes only, with no setback acceptable outcomes; setbacks for residential uses sit in the Residential activities code.

open_questions: Scope of Table 9.3.6.3 note 'the Queensland Development Code setbacks apply for dwelling houses and dual occupancies': does it displace AO 4.1 road setbacks as well as AO 4.2 side/rear, and does it reach Class 10a outbuildings ancillary to a dwelling house? Default reading: yes for side/rear, so dwelling-house outbuildings use QDC; all AO 4.1/4.2 rules flagged needs_manual_review.

Table 5.7.1 makes Class 10a building work in the Township zone accepted subject to PO 22/PO 23, but s1.6(4) lists only Low density and Medium density residential zones as containing building assessment provisions.
Table 9.3.6.3 lot-width bands are drafted as 'Not greater than 12.5 metres, but less than 15.0 metres' and 'Not greater than 15.0 metres, but less than 20 metres' (presumably 'greater than').

Grouping of 'If ...' conditions in the Part 5 tables (e.g. whether the 50m2 expansion condition attaches to Dwelling house in Local centre, Principal centre and Mixed use) is ambiguous in the PDF layout.
